answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy binds each identity to a non-transferable stake, not a free keypair. Registration needs proof-of-personhood attestation plus a bonded deposit, slashed once two identities are proven to share one operator, spotted by an identical timing pulse in transaction pacing or overlapping behavioral fingerprints. A farm must post a separate bond per clone, so forging N agents costs N bonds plus the collateral lost when one detection exposes a cluster. Reputation in the meadow of open tasks accrues only to bonded accounts, a haven clones cannot rent.
